questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to deal with a difficult or unfair boss at work
Why managers in big companies are paid so much
How tomatoes are grown and packed in California
Companies without managers, and the pros and cons
questions.why: They hear from companies that got rid of managers and discuss the possible problems.

questions.q: According to Neil, why do people often have problems with a boss?
options: Bosses are usually paid too much
Workers feel managers don't listen to them
Bosses change jobs too often
Workers don't want to work in teams
questions.why: Neil says this often happens because workers feel they aren't listened to by managers.

questions.q: What was the first principle at Morning Star, according to Doug Kirkpatrick?
options: Nobody should use force or pressure on anyone else
Everyone must work exactly the same number of hours
Managers make all of the big decisions for the team
Workers should compete with each other for bonuses
questions.why: He says the first principle was that people should not use force or coercion against others.

questions.q: How do employees at Morning Star get things done?
options: They follow orders from senior members of staff
They hold a vote on every single task they do
They ask others to act, and those people respond
They hire outside managers to organise the work
questions.why: Neil says employees can't tell others what to do; everything is based on requesting and responding.

questions.q: What concern does Dina Newman raise?
options: The company may lose money without proper control
Customers may be unhappy with the slower service
Workers may earn less than at other companies
It may help strong workers and leave weak ones behind
questions.why: She asks if it empowers people who are already good and leaves behind those who are not.

questions.q: How does Doug Kirkpatrick respond to that concern?
options: He rejects it: everyone benefits from being heard
He agrees that it is a big and serious problem
He says weaker workers are politely asked to leave
He says it doesn't really matter to the business
questions.why: He isn't sure he accepts 'left behind' and says everyone benefits because their voice is respected.

questions.q: What downside of having no bosses does Neil mention?
options: Workers become lazy when nobody is watching them
Extra responsibility can mean more work and stress
Big decisions are often made far too quickly
Nobody keeps their promises to their colleagues
questions.why: Neil says the extra responsibility can create more work and stress.

questions.q: What does Georgina imply about working without a boss?
options: It always makes people happier
It is only suitable for small companies
If things go wrong, you can only blame yourself
It makes it easier to avoid mistakes
questions.why: She says if things go wrong, 'there's no-one to blame but yourself!'
